ui_bugs.issue: Gyroid TPMS still renders with sharp radial triangular spikes and large tearing holes at cell=6, 12, 18 and in Unit Cell mode. Fix attempt (marchingTets below/above split + double iso-surface +c/-c + analytic normals + res cap) did NOT eliminate the spikes/holes. Root cause is most likely (1) merging the +c and -c iso-surfaces without CAPPING the open boundary where the wall exits the bounding box -> the sheet is open along its silhouette and shading shows through, and (2) the marching-tetrahedra 2-below/2-above quad still winds the quad's diagonal inconsistently vs. its triangle-fan neighbour -> long stray triangles ('spikes') appear at saddle voxels. The isosurface also has no boundary-clip: any tet whose vertex lies outside a solid domain (e.g. above +HEIGHT/2) still emits triangles because the field is periodic and doesn't 'know' about the box. Recommend: (a) close/cap the wall on the six bounding faces (emit boundary polygons where c<=f<=+c crosses the wall), (b) verify quad diagonal is chosen by the edge that separates the two 'below' vertices (currently the code assumes A-C, A-D, B-D, B-C but the correct planar quad ordering depends on tetra edge topology; the two valid triangulations are (AC,AD,BD)+(AC,BD,BC) OR (AC,AD,BC)+(AD,BD,BC); wrong choice creates a bow-tie / spike), (c) alternatively fall back to marching-cubes with lookup table (js-marching-cubes) for TPMS.

issues: Purple/magenta specular highlights visible on some triangles inside the gyroid -> indicates back-face normal inversion (normalSign) is inconsistent between the two iso-surfaces or between adjacent triangles; a purely convex-lit blue material should never show that hue.

action_items: Gyroid bug still present. Re-implement TPMS iso-surface. Recommended approach: use a proper marching-cubes implementation (e.g. isosurface / marching-cubes-3d npm) OR fix the current marching-tets in two ways: (1) correct the 2v/2v quad triangulation so the shared diagonal is the edge between the two below-vertices' cuts, and (2) add DOMAIN-BOUNDARY CAPPING so the resulting mesh is watertight where the wall exits the bounding box (cap on x=+-extent, y=+-HEIGHT/2, z=+-extent).

Consider raising 'wall' contribution to 'c' (currently c = min(0.9, max(0.12, wall*k*1.3/2))) - at wall=0.5, cell=12: k=2pi/12=0.524, c=0.5*0.524*1.3/2=0.170 which is fine, but at cell=6 c grows to 0.34 and near-saturates. The bounded c is not the issue, but merging with capping IS.
Investigate purple/magenta highlights (likely normalSign mismatch between gA and gB sub-meshes).
STL file for gyroid is 43 MB - consider mesh decimation before export.
critical_code_review_comments: geometry.js buildGyroid merges two separate marching-tets outputs without any boundary capping - the resulting mesh is never watertight, which is why 'holes' appear at the silhouette.

marchingtets.js quad triangulation (A-C,A-D,B-D,B-C) is a plausible order but assumes a specific tetra vertex layout; the six tets in TETS have different local topologies so the same 2-below index pattern maps to different edge geometries. A single hardcoded diagonal will bow-tie roughly 1/6th of the quad cases, producing exactly the kind of long spikes visible.

normalSign is applied as a scalar divisor on the gradient magnitude (l = (|g|||1) * normalSign) which does NOT flip the normal direction - it only makes l negative and thus negates the components once, so it currently works, but is semantically fragile; safer to compute unit normal then multiply by normalSign.
resolution cap 'cap' of 56 combined with 24 in Y still produces 56*24*56*6 tets ~= 450k -> ~1M triangles for the wall; expensive and explains the 43MB STL. Consider marching-cubes at 48^3.
Viewer3D still has no error boundary for geometry build failures; a bad iso-surface would show a blank canvas without user feedback.

rca of the issue: Gyroid TPMS is built by running marchingTets twice (iso = +c and iso = -c) and merging the two open sheets. Two structural problems remain: (1) neither sheet is closed at the bounding-box faces, so the mesh has open perimeters that show as 'holes' when viewed from an angle; (2) the 2-below/2-above tetra case emits a fixed diagonal (A-C ; A-D ; B-D ; B-C) but the six tets that decompose a cube have different local vertex layouts, so on ~1/6 of the quad cases the diagonal bow-ties, producing the long triangular 'spikes' the user reported. The 'fix' addressed part of the winding but did not add domain capping nor topology-aware diagonal selection. Reproduction: open https://dynamiccoreai.preview.emergentagent.com/?pattern=gyroid&cell=18 and observe sharp cones on the outline plus obvious black holes through the sheet. Mitigation: switch iso-surfacing to a marching-cubes implementation (deterministic 256-case table) and add boundary capping OR fix diagonal selection per-tet.
